rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes `col < N` to `col <= N` on line 19. With N=4096 and the grid configuration yielding grid_size=(256,256) with block_size=(16,16), the maximum possible column index is 255*16+15=4095. Since col can only range from 0 to 4095, the condition `col < 4096` is always true for all launched threads, and so is `col <= 4096`. The only difference between the two predicates would occur when col==4096, but this value is never reached by any thread in the kernel launch configuration. Therefore, both the original and mutated code follow identical execution paths for every thread, producing identical results regardless of input tensor values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shape contract. The grid/block launch parameters guarantee col∈[0,4095], making both col<4096 and col<=4096 always true. No input values can make col==N reachable since thread indices are determined by launch configuration, not by tensor values.
rounds.recommendations: When testing relational operator mutations in CUDA kernels, analyze grid/block launch parameters to determine actual thread index ranges. Mutations to boundary conditions are often equivalent when the grid is sized exactly to the data dimensions (N divisible by block size) or when ceiling division ensures no threads reach the boundary case.
